intro: No named consent management platform was detected on this site, or a custom implementation is in use. Fixes will typically require a developer and, if third-party tags are managed via a tag manager like Google Tag Manager, a tag manager admin.

sections.title: Option A — Install a consent management platform
steps: The most reliable path to compliance is to install a recognised CMP (OneTrust, Cookiebot, CookieYes, Usercentrics, or similar). These platforms handle the banner UI, consent record storage, and script blocking in one solution.
Choose a CMP that supports UK GDPR and PECR. Confirm it stores consent records with a timestamp and purpose, and blocks non-essential scripts before consent.
After installation, configure each cookie category and map your third-party scripts to the appropriate categories.

sections.title: Option B — Gate scripts manually via Google Tag Manager
steps: If you use Google Tag Manager, enable Google Consent Mode v2 in your GTM container.
Add a consent initialisation tag that sets default denied states: analytics_storage=denied, ad_storage=denied, functionality_storage=denied. This tag must fire before all other tags.
Your cookie banner must update these signals when the user accepts or rejects. Each GTM tag must have a 'Consent Check' trigger that requires the relevant signal to be 'granted' before firing.
Never use 'Page View' as the only trigger for analytics or advertising tags — this fires before consent is given.

sections.title: Option C — Block scripts directly in site code
steps: For sites without a tag manager: change non-essential script tags from <script src='...'> to <script type='text/plain' data-category='analytics' src='...'>.
After the user consents, your consent handler must dynamically re-create the script tags with type='text/javascript' for the accepted categories.
Store the consent choice in a first-party cookie (e.g. cookies_policy='{"analytics":true,"advertising":false}'). On subsequent page loads, read this cookie and activate the appropriate scripts.
Ensure the stored consent record is checked before any non-essential code runs — not just on the page where the banner appears.

sections.title: Confirm the banner meets first-layer parity
steps: The banner's first visible layer must give equal prominence to 'Accept' and 'Reject'. If your banner shows 'Accept all' with a large button but only a small text link for 'Manage preferences', this does not meet ICO guidance.
Add a 'Reject all' button to the first layer. It should be the same visual size and contrast as 'Accept all'.
Do not pre-tick checkboxes in a preference centre. All non-essential categories must default to off.
